title: ところで — “by the way”
summary: ところで is a conjunction used at the start of a sentence to change the topic: “by the way.” It moves from the current subject to a new one, often a question. It is used in conversation, emails and speeches.

patterns.form: ところで、〜（質問・新しい話題）
patterns.gloss: ところで + new topic or question

body.p: ところで signals a change of subject. After a conversation has finished or slowed down, you can bring up what you really wanted to say: ところで、最近忙しいですか. It marks a clear break from the previous topic.
It always comes at the start of a sentence, followed by a comma. What follows is something not connected, or only loosely connected, with what came before.

body.h: Do not confuse with ところが / ところで (conditional)
body.p: ところで after a verb ta-form (例: 謝ったところで) is a different pattern meaning “even if.” The topic-changing ところで stands alone at the start of the sentence.

examples.ja: ところで、最近（さいきん）忙（いそが）しいですか。
examples.romaji: Tokoro de, saikin isogashii desu ka.
examples.tr: By the way, have you been busy lately?

examples.ja: ところで、あの本（ほん）はもう読（よ）み終（お）わりましたか。
examples.romaji: Tokoro de, ano hon wa mō yomiowarimashita ka.
examples.tr: By the way, have you finished reading that book yet?

examples.ja: ところで、週末（しゅうまつ）の予定（よてい）はもう決（き）まりましたか。
examples.romaji: Tokoro de, shūmatsu no yotei wa mō kimarimashita ka.
examples.tr: By the way, have your weekend plans been decided yet?

pitfalls: Do not use it to continue the same topic. For adding to the same topic, use それに or また.
Do not confuse it with ところが (however) or the ta-form + ところで (even if).
